get.description: Return the home Pulse: a snapshot recomputed per request from journal state. Only the new-owner onboarding signals are named in this contract — journal_age_days, home_state, and welcome_framing; the rest of the payload is intentionally open and may change without a contract bump.

example.welcome_framing: most of what i keep becomes useful after about a week, once your journal has enough of your days in it to show patterns. for now, here's what's already happening:

home_state.description: Home onboarding posture: 'welcome' until the home surface has any narrative, activity, anticipated item, briefing, attention item, pulse need, or weekly reflection; 'active' once any exists.

journal_age_days.description: Whole days from the earliest chronicle day to today; 0 when no chronicle day exists yet.

welcome_framing.description: First-week framing line for new owners: the framing text when home_state is 'welcome' and journal_age_days <= 7, otherwise null.

200.description: Home Pulse snapshot. Fields beyond the three named here are present but not contracted.

post.description: Upload one capture segment from a linked device as multipart form data. Identity is the linked-device mTLS certificate. The body has one JSON `envelope` part plus repeated `files` parts. Envelope grammar is `core/crates/solstone-core/src/contract/schemas/protocol.schema.json` (required `day`, `segment`, `files`; optional `source`, `meta`; `stream` and `observer` are forbidden). Each multipart part is at most 64 MiB; the total request is at most 128 MiB.

parameters.description: Linked-device ingest protocol version. Must be 3. Values less than 3 are rejected with HTTP 426 Upgrade Required; values greater than 3 are rejected as unsupported. Identity is the linked-device mTLS certificate, not a request header.
parameters.name: X-Solstone-Protocol-Version

413.description: Request exceeds the 128 MiB total-body limit.

delete.description: Erase every journal segment that holds location.jsonl as a whole segment, leaving tombstone.json. Removal runs only through retention's door; this route selects the set. mixed_segments is a cost disclosure, never a disposition: mixed segments are still removed whole. Authorization is derived from AccessBasis::LinkedDevice, established by the paired-device TLS client certificate; no bearer token or request header is accepted. The receipt includes removed.tombstones and does not include removed.in_segment_derived.

400.description: Only the supported `location` source can be deleted.

403.description: A linked-device certificate identity is required. Localhost, pairing peers, and missing identities are refused; a revoked linked device is refused by the authorization gate.

503.description: The location-mutation lock could not be acquired; no deletion was performed.
